criteria_results.criterion: Head identifies the missing named capability, performs one bounded acquisition and replans with an actually qualified local procedure.
criteria_results.notes: Both parts agree. observation.json names observation-digest-v1 as the missing capability and records one bounded acquisition of a stdlib-only Node procedure at a stable in-workspace path (bin/observation-digest-v1.js, sha256 8daae21f...), matching the host manifest. The host gate released only the exact qualified command and refused other forms, showing host-side qualification and a replan onto that procedure. Part 2 corroborates real behaviour with three distinct input-rejection cases (non-integer value, empty observations array, malformed JSON) and a scheduled=0 edge case producing a coherent zero-total digest. Caveat noted by both parts: qualification is producer-run, mitigated by independent hand arithmetic in verification/.

criteria_results.criterion: The acquired procedure is invoked with its exact qualified executable bytes and fixed arguments; a durable invocation receipt is present.
criteria_results.notes: Both parts pass. invocation-receipt.json is registered and present (5920 B, sha256 98671781...586f per host registry), recording attempt ID, executable path and sha256 (8daae21f..., gate-verified and matching the host manifest), exit 0, empty stderr, invocation_count 1, and the two positional args in the spec's exact order. The output directory is the workspace root, not a probe directory. The `--` token in argv is a Node option terminator forced by the host gate, never reaches the procedure, and the two positional arguments remain exact. Indirect byte evidence is strong: final digest.json and digest.md hashes equal the hashes of outputs produced by the procedure in probe/out and probe/out2, so registered bytes are the procedure's own output rather than hand-written.

criteria_results.criterion: digest.json has exact numeric row_count, scheduled, completed, incidents, completion_percent (2 decimals), and a sites object keyed by site with totals; digest.md presents the same values with a reproducible method.
criteria_results.notes: Both parts independently recomputed from the fixture rows (North/Harbor 12,11,2; South/Harbor 8,8,1; North/Ridge 10,7,3): row_count 3; scheduled 30; completed 26; incidents 6; 26/30 = 86.666... -> 86.67 (half-up, not truncation); North 2 rows, 22/18/5, 18/22 = 81.818... -> 81.82; South 1 row, 8/8/1, 100.00. digest.json matches on every field, all values are JSON numbers, sites is an object keyed North and South with totals, and site sums reconcile (2+1=3, 22+8=30, 18+8=26, 5+1=6). digest.md renders the same values with a documented 7-step method covering input shape, pooled formula, half-up rounding, zero-denominator rule and cross-checks; the pooled formula is used rather than an unweighted mean of site percentages. Its hash cfbdcf29...99e8 matches the host manifest and the probe copies.

criteria_results.criterion: All deliverables are registered artifacts whose bytes pass independent host verification and independent Nox QA.
criteria_results.notes: Both parts pass. The host candidate registry lists every deliverable with a host-computed sha256 and size: digest.json 571d8fd2...1099 (477 B, rev 2), digest.md cfbdcf29...99e8 (1516 B, rev 2), invocation-receipt.json 98671781...586f, both verification reports (rev 2) and the probe evidence. The two digest hashes equal the hashes of independently-run probe outputs, giving meaningful byte-level corroboration that the final artifacts are the procedure's output and were not edited afterwards. Independent Nox QA is this review. Remaining blemishes are non-blocking: producer reports leave three hashes null (the host supplies them), and stated sizes for digest.md read 1514 B against the host's 1516 B.

defects.issue: Several byte sizes appear to be character counts rather than UTF-8 byte lengths: the receipt, analyst and registration records and qa-summary state digest.md as 1514 bytes while the host manifest and probe copies record 1516 for the same sha256 (em dash encodes as 3 bytes), and the registration record gives verification/independent-verification.md as 10241 against a host value of 10412. The 'bytes_unchanged' / 'byte-identical' evidence therefore rests on inaccurate counts, though no content difference is implied since hashes agree.

digest.md's method section says 'Read the fixture JSON' without naming input/pilot.observations.json, so a reader holding only digest.md must infer the input locator. All other method elements (input shape, pooled formula, half-up rounding, zero-denominator rule, cross-checks) are present and correct, and the procedure's fixed positional arguments make the numbers reproducible.

No role in the run recomputed any hash: the qa-summary records sha256 as null for invocation-receipt.json and both verification reports and labels only the two digest hashes as procedure-reported. The host registry does carry hashes for all of them, but the producers' own evidence on its face is incomplete for criterion 4.

sites.South.completion_percent is serialized as the JSON literal 100 while digest.md renders 100.00. The value is numerically correct, the 2-decimal requirement applies to the top-level field (86.67), and JSON numbers cannot carry fixed scale without breaking the numeric-typing requirement. Representational only, correctly flagged rather than hidden.

The invocation receipt's timestamp (2026-11-16T11:35:29Z) is derived from the epoch embedded in the mission report directory name rather than read from a clock, because the shell was gated to the single node command and refused `date`. Disclosed and labelled a lower bound, but it is not an observed invocation time.

The analyst quoted verification-report sha256 prefixes 73aab63e... / 04100c3a..., while the final manifest shows revision 2 with 5a345a73... / 16c154dd..., suggesting the report bytes changed when re-registered. Consistent with the revision bump; no downstream artifact depends on these hashes.

Negative-test claims for 'relative input path' and 'missing arguments' have no corresponding artifacts, and the bad*.err contents were not shown in part 1 (part 2 did confirm bad1/bad2/bad3 error cases).

recommendations: Record byte sizes as UTF-8 byte lengths, not character counts, in receipts, registration records and close-out summaries, and reconcile the 1514 vs 1516 digest.md figure.

Add the fixture path (input/pilot.observations.json) to the digest.md method section so the document is self-contained, ideally by parameterizing the procedure rather than hand-editing generated output.
Have the host or a verifier with shell access recompute sha256 for every registered artifact and populate the receipt and reports instead of leaving nulls.
Explain in the close-out why the verification-report sha256 changed between the analyst's save and revision 2, so the content-identical claim is corroborated.
Capture the real invocation timestamp from host-side instrumentation keyed to gate release instead of deriving it from the directory-name epoch.

Store a machine-readable expected-values source derived independently of the procedure (or the analyst's hand-arithmetic transcript) alongside the probe evidence, so qualification is not validated solely by the producer's own expected numbers.
review.verdict: PASS: PASS: Both parts independently recomputed the digest values from the fixture bytes and confirmed row_count 3, scheduled 30, completed 26, incidents 6, completion_percent 86.67 (half-up), and per-site totals (North 81.82, South 100.00) matching digest.json and digest.md; the acquired observation-digest-v1 procedure sits at a stable in-workspace path with bytes matching the host manifest, was invoked with the exact fixed positional arguments under a reproducible receipt, and all deliverables are host-registered artifacts whose hashes equal the procedure's own probe-run outputs. Remaining defects are documentation and bookkeeping minors (byte-size counts, unnamed fixture path in the method text, null self-reported hashes, derived timestamp) that do not affect the numeric results or artifact integrity.
